correctness.rationale: The diameter set consists of finitely many strictly exposed ordered vertex pairs. Positive cone heights prove uniform localization at scale t. A radial Taylor expansion has uniformly bounded O(t^2) remainder and the leading product-cone integral is an exact beta integral. Dirichlet(d,d,1) heights yield the explicit second coefficient, positive as a transverse squared-distance expectation. Orthotope formulas are verified a second way via triangular coordinate-difference densities. Executed verifier: 1,838 tests, including 1,818 exact orthotope instances, 16 regular-simplex cases and four independent direct quadrature comparisons.

originality.rationale: Searches and selected primary texts found the general pair-distance distribution variational theory (Wang), planar polygon exact distributions (Pure et al.), and mean-distance inequalities (Bonnet et al.), but not the dimension >=3 local cone-moment second-order theorem or the sharp orthotope relative-correction rigidity. Earlier regular-simplex instances are subsumed and explicitly not independently novel. Schrempp (arXiv:1709.03706) and earlier papers on maxima of large random point samples include cube leading-order information but not the fixed-two-point arbitrary-polytope second-order coefficient. The possible absence of an indexed treatment cannot establish historical uniqueness; equivalence priority risk is recorded.
residual_risks: An equivalent asymptotic may exist in older unindexed extreme-value or convex-geometric probability literature; in particular, leading near-diameter cube behavior already informs prior many-point diameter limits.
General covariogram integral identities and older unindexed works might implicitly yield an equivalent expansion even when the published comparison does not explicitly evaluate it.
Semantic searches and a partition by mathematical topic do not certify uniqueness.

value.rationale: Gives a complete universal leading and next-to-leading extreme-pair-distance law for all d>=3 polytopes, with coefficients computable solely from tangent-cone volumes and two elementary transverse moments. Exponent 2d and positivity supply structural information, while the independent orthotope formula yields a sharp fixed-diameter rigidity theorem uniquely selecting cubes. No larger downstream theorem is needed for this natural endpoint invariant.
